sources_considered.why: Read the paper. It argues against incremental LLM development reaching human-capable AGI while expressly allowing LLMs as components of broader systems.
Read the abstract and publication history. Relevant experiments and an opposing interpretation of GPT-4's general capabilities.
Read the abstract. Its specific computational limits and assumptions do not establish the broader AGI impossibility claim.
Read the announcement when checking later developments. It concerns a later model and company-reported benchmark results, not independent proof about the June 2024 systems or an agreed AGI threshold.

evidence_items.explanation: The paper argues that contemporary interactive LLMs alone are not a practical route to human-capable AGI, but allows them as components of broader architectures. That distinction prevents using this skeptical analysis as proof of Zitron's unqualified impossibility claim.

The authors report broad capabilities and interpret GPT-4 as an incomplete early form of AGI. Their experiments challenge a categorical dismissal, but neither selected tasks nor that interpretation establish complete AGI or prove future feasibility.

unresolved_gaps: No applicable impossibility proof or independently validated qualifying AGI was established by the reviewed evidence.
The boundary between the existing generative approach and a materially different architecture is unspecified.
No evidence establishes that computing technology unavailable in June 2024 is necessary.
